changes.before: What does applying the reference to "trail" return?
changes.after: Use an existing method as an operation to call later.

before: A method reference such as Main::length adapts an existing compatible method to a functional interface. It does not call the method immediately. ToIntFunction<String> has applyAsInt(String).
The referenced static method takes a String and returns an int, matching the target contract. A lambda text -> length(text) expresses the same delegation here.
Expected output or behavior: 3. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Rewrite the reference as an equivalent lambda. You may trace it without a JDK; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A method reference points to an existing method that can do a job later. Main::length refers to Main's length method. Creating this reference does not run the method or store an answer.
The target interface, ToIntFunction<String>, needs an operation that takes a String and returns an int. length fits those types. Calling applyAsInt later passes its input to that method.
The program prints 3. length receives map and returns its length of three UTF-16 units.
The quiz supplies different text. The method runs with that new input; it does not reuse an earlier answer.
